subject: Computer Networking
title: The Telephone Network
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Telephone Network.

hook.text: In 1876, Bell spoke into a wire and his assistant heard him in the next room. Voice over wire changed everything.

buildup.text: Telephone exchanges connected callers through switchboards. Human operators physically plugged wires together.

discovery.text: The phone system became the largest engineered network in history — circuit-switched and globally connected.

twist.text: Circuit switching reserved a dedicated line for each call. If the line was busy, you simply couldn't connect.

climax.text: This network carried only voice for a century. Nobody imagined it could carry data — until modems came along.

punchline.text: The phone network proved global connectivity was possible.

quiz.question: What switching method did early telephone networks use?

details.summary: The telephone network, built from the 1870s onward, created the first circuit-switched communication infrastructure. Calls established a dedicated connection between two endpoints.
details.whyItMatters: The telephone network built the physical infrastructure and switching concepts that the internet later repurposed. Dial-up internet literally ran on telephone lines.
takeaways: Circuit switching dedicates a path for each conversation
The phone network built the wiring infrastructure reused by the internet
Telephone exchanges pioneered automated switching technology

faq.question: What is circuit switching and why does it matter?
faq.answer: Circuit switching creates a dedicated path between two endpoints for the duration of a call. It guarantees consistent quality but wastes capacity when nobody is talking. The internet's packet switching solved this inefficiency by sharing capacity dynamically.

faq.question: How did the telephone network enable the internet?
faq.answer: The copper telephone lines reaching every home provided the physical connection for dial-up modems. The telephone network's infrastructure of switches, exchanges, and long-distance lines were repurposed for data. DSL technology later sent internet data over the same phone wires.
